newsitem.title: UK: UK says water crisis plan gets positive response.
newsitem.headline: UK says water crisis plan gets positive response.

text.p: British water and sewerage companies have generally responded positively to a 10-point plan drawn up to tackle current industry problems by the new Labour government, deputy prime minister John Prescott said on Tuesday.
"I think they've responded in a positive way and I'm able to say we're well on the way to establishing a national strategy for water supply and quality," Prescott told BBC radio.
Prescott said there were "one or two" exceptions which the government was still talking to.
He said he could now see a way to cut leakage, which had seen around 30 percent of supplies seeping out of pipes.
Mandatory targets to cut leaks were a key part of the plan, announced at a crisis summit in May as the country emerged from its driest period in 200 years.
"They have responded positively and so will I," Prescott said.
He said there were still some problems over groundwater supplies, which are at very low levels in much of the country, and extraction rates.
Prescott said he would be announcing some proposals for those later on Tuesday. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
